From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme trial procurement & billing  next steps

Hi Alice  thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

1) Recap:
- Goal: validate eval workload (chat-based customer support generation) across a 4-week trial. Success criteria: 90% intent-match on evaluation prompts and cost per 1k tokens under your target (TBD).
- Target trial load: ~500k tokens/week for first two weeks, potential ramp to ~1.5M tokens/week in week 3 if initial metrics look good.

2) Procurement & commercial path questions:
- Preferred payment method: PO/invoice vs corporate card? You mentioned procurement handles PO requests  can you confirm the billing flow and required PO language?
- Marketplace interest: would you prefer to procure via AWS Marketplace (metered billing) or direct Redwood invoice? Marketplace can simplify procurement but changes invoicing cadence.

3) Trial-to-paid triggers & billing start:
- We typically start billing when either: (a) trial ends and customer opts in, or (b) an agreed usage threshold is exceeded and you want to convert early. If you prefer automatic conversion on threshold, we can add that to the SOW/ordering docs. What would you consider the conversion trigger (e.g., sustained >1M tokens/week or reaching X successful conversations)?

4) Next steps / timeline:
- Can procurement share required PO template and expected legal review timeline?
- I will follow up with a draft SOW/ordering doc and an estimate for a 3-month post-trial commitment for pricing planning.

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-Acme-20260506.pdf (mutual action plan)

If you can send the PO template or preferred invoicing contact, Ill loop in our contracts team and get a draft over by EOD Friday.

Thanks 
Marissa

Subject: Re: Acme trial procurement & billing  next steps

Hi Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from procurement/legal side: 

- Payment method: Acme prefers PO/invoice for anything over $10k. For pilot projects we can sometimes do card, but PO is the default. We will issue a PO with standard Acme terms; I attached our procurement checklist and PO template.
- PO language: we need vendor legal name, address, remit-to, and our standard IP/data processing clause. I dont expect intellectual property objections for this pilot but legal will confirm within 5 business days.
- Marketplace: we prefer direct vendor invoice for pilots to keep billing predictable. Marketplace is something the platform team may evaluate later.
- Conversion trigger: procurement is comfortable with conversion on customer confirmation after the 4-week trial. From product/ops wed like a hard usage threshold only if Redwood can provide automatic ceilings and alerts. For now, we propose manual conversion after a joint review call.

Timeline: legal review ~5 business days after we receive the SOW and ordering docs. Procurement can sign a PO within 3 business days after legal clears.

Attachments: Acme_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (procurement checklist)

Best,
Alice Lawson
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
alice.lawson@acme.com
